summary: Lists requirements for managing equipment in MPLS-TP networks, in terms of the management capabilities the protocol building blocks must offer. It does not say what a particular implementation must support. It is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: A checklist of what control panel buttons a transport network needs so operators can look after it.

questions: what is a defect versus a failure in mpls-tp
subtitle: A checklist of the fault, configuration, performance and security management features that MPLS-TP equipment needs to offer.

tldr.problem: MPLS-TP is meant to give packet networks the behaviour of a transport network, and operators need a common set of management capabilities to run such equipment.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists numbered requirements, using MUST, SHOULD and MAY, for management interfaces, fault handling, configuration, performance measurement and security of an MPLS-TP network element.
tldr.outcome: It sets what management specifications must cover, without choosing a management protocol or saying what any one product supports. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 5951 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is a requirements document, so it states what management specifications must cover and leaves details such as default timer values to them.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 5951 specifies the requirements for managing equipment in networks that support the MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP). The requirements are written for the people who specify the protocol mechanisms and procedures that MPLS-TP is built from. They say what management capabilities MPLS must offer so that MPLS-TP can be managed.

The document is explicit that it identifies essential capabilities and does not say what functions any particular MPLS implementation supports. It builds on ITU-T G.7710/Y.1701 and RFC 4377, and the authors assume the reader knows RFC 5921 and RFC 5950.

Although it is not a protocol specification, it uses the RFC 2119 key words to tell protocol designers what their solutions have to satisfy.
sections.eli5: This is a list of what a control panel for a transport network must be able to do. It does not say which brand of panel to buy.

sections.title: Key Terms
sections.content:
The RFC defines a vocabulary of fault terms that later sections rely on. An anomaly is the smallest observable discrepancy. When anomalies become dense enough to interrupt a required function, that is a defect. A fault cause is the result of correlating defects to find the one that represents the disturbance. A failure is a fault cause that persisted long enough to consider the function terminated.

On the communications side, a Communication Channel (CCh) is a logical channel between network elements. The Management Communication Channel (MCC) is a CCh dedicated to management, and the Signaling Communication Channel (SCC) is one dedicated to control plane messages. The networks that carry them are the MCN and SCN. An Operations System (OS) is the system that supports operations, administration and maintenance.

OAM can run on-demand (started by hand for a limited time to run diagnostics) or proactive (carried on continuously to permit timely reporting).
sections.eli5: A small glitch is a hiccup, many hiccups in a row are a defect, and a problem that will not go away is a failure. Operators only want to be called about the last one.

sections.title: Management Interfaces and Channels
sections.content:
The RFC does not pick a standard management protocol. It allows an end-to-end connection to cross domains where one is managed with NETCONF or SNMP and another with CORBA. A network element MAY support more than one management protocol at once, for example one for configuration and another for monitoring, at the operator's discretion.

Every MPLS-TP network element MUST connect to an OS, either directly or indirectly through another network element. In the indirect case, an MCC MUST be supported between the two elements. Specifications SHOULD also define management connectivity with remote domains and with elements under a third-party operator.

The management network (MCN) MUST meet the ITU-T G.7712 requirements for CCh access, data-link termination, encapsulation, forwarding, interworking, tunneling and routing. It also needs management functions of its own: retrieving DCN parameters such as packet size, timeouts and window size, establishing message routing, managing DCN addresses, reading the DCN's operational status, and enabling or disabling an element's access to the DCN so a malfunctioning element can be isolated. RFC 5586 defines the Generic Associated Channel used to realize a CCh, and RFC 5718 describes how it forms part of the MCN and SCN.
sections.eli5: Every device must be wired to the control room, directly or by passing messages through a neighbour. The RFC does not say which language the control room must speak.

sections.title: Fault Management
sections.content:
Fault management covers supervision, detection, validation, isolation, correction and reporting of abnormal operation. A network element MUST supervise the OAM mechanisms in use (those required by RFC 5860), loop checking and failure detection on the data-plane forwarding path, and software problems such as out-of-memory conditions. It MUST also supervise hardware problems with units, cables and power, and SHOULD supervise the environment, for example temperature and humidity. Path supervision MUST be configurable as on-demand or proactive.

Validation turns short-lived fault causes into reportable failures. The element MUST run persistency checks first. A path failure MUST be declared if the fault cause persists continuously for a configurable time (Time-D) and cleared if it is absent continuously for a configurable time (Time-C). As an example, the text suggests defaults of 2.5 +/- 0.5 seconds and 10 +/- 0.5 seconds, taken from G.7710. Declaring and clearing a failure MUST be time stamped.

For alarms, the element SHOULD allow severities such as Critical, Major, Minor and Warning to be assigned by configuration, MUST support configured alarm suppression, MUST report alarms locally and to an OS, and SHOULD support Alarm Reporting Control, which switches reporting off for one managed entity (for example an LSP) during testing and back on once it is ready. An element carrying other technologies over MPLS-TP MUST translate MPLS-TP defects into failures meaningful to the client layer.
sections.eli5: A smoke alarm should not ring for one puff of steam. The device waits to be sure the problem is real, notes the time, then raises the alarm and can be told how loud to make it.

sections.title: Configuration Management
sections.content:
Configuration management covers hardware and software setup, transport paths including working and protection paths, and the OAM that checks them. The element MUST support the G.7710 configuration requirements for hardware, software and the local real-time clock, including alignment with an external time reference.

If a control plane exists, the management plane MUST be able to configure it. The element MUST support static provisioning of transport paths, configuration of performance thresholds such as Loss Measurement and Delay Measurement thresholds, and configuration of LSP information. If the control plane supports handing LSP setup from management to control plane, the hand-off MUST be manageable. Further detail is left to the specifications for the MPLS-TP control plane.

For protection, the element MUST allow LSPs to be designated as working or protecting, associations between them to be defined, and manual switching, forced switching and protection lockout to be operated and released. It MUST also allow setting Automatic Protection Switching parameters including Wait to Restore time and protection switching thresholds.

For OAM, the element MUST let operators choose which functions are enabled, tie them to specific maintenance entities, set them up as part of LSP setup and tear-down, and configure identifiers such as MEP ID and MIP ID for connectivity checking. OAM runs as one-time on-demand (immediate or pre-scheduled), periodic on-demand, or proactive ongoing.
sections.eli5: Operators must be able to set up the roads, name the spare road to use when one is blocked, and choose when the road inspectors do their rounds.

sections.title: Performance Management
sections.content:
Performance management supports maintenance, bring-into-service, quality of service and statistics gathering. It must be possible to tell when an MPLS-TP transport service is available and when it is not. The RFC defines a service as unavailable when performance has degraded past a configurable threshold and stayed there long enough to rule out a measurement anomaly. How unavailability is calculated from raw data is out of scope, but the management information model MUST include objects for the availability state of services. Unavailability is based on Severely Errored Seconds (SES) and Unavailable Seconds (UAS).

The element MUST collect loss measurement and delay measurement statistics, report performance degradation through fault management (for example to trigger protection switching or to prompt a repair), and report statistics on request from a management system.

The scope of measurement depends on the connection type. For bidirectional point-to-point connections, on-demand single-ended loss measurement and proactive loss measurement in each direction are REQUIRED. For unidirectional connections, proactive loss measurement is REQUIRED, and on-demand delay measurement is REQUIRED. Co-routed bidirectional connections need on-demand one-way and two-way delay, and associated bidirectional ones need on-demand one-way delay.
sections.eli5: The network must keep score of how much traffic gets lost and how long it takes, and say clearly whether the service is working or not.

sections.title: Security Management Requirements
sections.content:
A network element MUST support secure management and control planes. Secure channels MUST be supported for all traffic and protocols used for management, at least those for configuration, monitoring, configuration backup, logging, time synchronization, authentication and routing. The MCC MUST support application protocols that give confidentiality and data-integrity protection.

The element MUST support open cryptographic algorithms (see RFC 3871), authentication so that only authenticated entities can manage it, authorization such as an Access Control List, and port access control so that management activity is accepted only on an authorized management port.

Security for the signaling channel is driven by similar considerations, but control plane security is left to the control plane specifications. For denial of service, an element MUST support secure management protocols and SHOULD do so in a way that limits the impact of an attack, and SHOULD offer further mitigation that lets it keep meeting its primary functions. The Security Considerations section adds that solutions MUST prevent unauthorized or unauthenticated access, and notes that diagnostics and path characterization expose network construction details that an operator may consider private.
sections.eli5: Only people with the right key may use the control panel, their messages must be private and untampered, and the panel must not fall over if someone spams it.
